h1: Best Western Royal Buriram Hotel — an international-brand hotel in central Buriram that puts everything a few minutes' drive away
intro: If you're coming to Buriram and want a hotel with international-brand standards but don't want to pay luxury-resort prices — Best Western Royal Buriram Hotel is one of the first names that comes to mind for a lot of people · It's a 3-star hotel under Best Western International, set on Jira Road in the city centre, near the Lower Isan Cultural Centre and the King Rama I Monument · The property is two bright-design four-storey buildings, with marble-floored rooms, an outdoor saltwater pool and spacious free parking · 79 rooms, from about THB 1,100/night · scores 8.2 on Trip.com and 4.1/5 on TripAdvisor from 190 reviews, ranking #3 of 23 hotels in Buriram.

body.html: Who Best Western Royal Buriram suits — to put it as simply as possible, this is a hotel for people who want "the reassurance of an international brand at local prices" in central Buriram · It isn't a luxury stadium-side hotel like the one football fans pick, and it isn't a tiny boutique selling quiet — it's a 3-star hotel under Best Western International that's been open since 2013 and is still running as usual · What makes people choose it is the familiar brand name, predictable room standards, and a city-centre location that puts the main sights a few minutes' drive away · Real reviews line up on who fits here: business travellers in town for meetings or work, families road-tripping around Lower Isan who want a place with easy parking, and visitors coming for the football or the racing who'd rather stay in the city than right by the stadium · Another group that says they're happy is people who've stayed at Best Western hotels elsewhere and know what to expect, because this one gives the same standard feel · On the flip side, if you're after the slick design of a newer hotel or full resort-style facilities, this place might look a little plain, because the main draws are value and location, not flash.

Location and getting around — the hotel is located at 332/22-23 Jira Road, Nai Muang Subdistrict, Muang Buriram District, which really is in the city centre, not the outskirts · What a lot of people like is how close it is to several key spots: the King Rama I Monument is about 1.3 kilometres away, an easy walk on a nice day, while the Lower Isan Cultural Centre (Buriram Rajabhat University) is about 2.4 kilometres away, or roughly a 6–8 min drive · Buriram railway station is about 2.7 kilometres away, a few minutes by car — handy if you've come in by train and just need a short hop · Seraka Market, the night market and restaurants in town are also a short drive away, so heading out for dinner in the evening is no trouble · Chang Arena and the Chang International Circuit sit out toward the edge of town, about a 10–15 min drive, so for people coming for the football or the racing who still want to sleep in the city, this is a good middle ground · The honest note is that the area's "walkability" is roughly middling — some spots are walkable, but plenty still need a car, especially at night when the footpaths and street lighting aren't bright on every soi, so if you're not driving yourself, have the Grab app or a taxi number ready.

"We drove down to tour Lower Isan and chose this place because it has wide free parking and sits in the city, so everything is close · The room was clean, the air-con was nicely cold, and in the morning we'd go down for breakfast and then drive straight on to the temples with no fuss. Great value for the brand name."

Room types and decor — Best Western Royal Buriram has 79 rooms in total, spread across two four-storey buildings designed to feel bright with easy-on-the-eye tones · The main rooms break down into Standard King, Standard Twin and Deluxe King, most of them non-smoking · What sets the rooms here apart from same-priced hotels in town is the marble floors, which feel clean and are easy to maintain, plus a small sitting area in the room, a fridge/minibar, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, tea- and coffee-making gear, and free Wi-Fi · Bathrooms are shower-type with basic free toiletries · Plenty of reviews agree the rooms are bigger than expected and clean, the beds are comfy, and the air-con cools fast, which matters a lot in Buriram's heat · For families there's a Family room option, good for anyone travelling with kids · A small thing some reviews mention is that the building's lift is fairly small, so if you're a big group with large bags you may have to split up, and some rooms on the road-facing side or lower floors catch a bit of traffic noise during the day · Overall the rooms here are good for a 3-star upcountry hotel and give the international-standard feel the brand name implies.

Facilities and the pool — the highlight that comes up often is the outdoor saltwater pool in the hotel's common area · A saltwater pool is something a lot of people like because it's gentler on the skin and eyes than a typical chlorine pool, good for kids to splash in and for adults to soak and cool off after a full day of driving around · There are seating spots around the pool to relax · Beyond the pool, the hotel also has free on-site parking, which is a big advantage for people road-tripping around Lower Isan, because finding a city-centre place with parking this convenient isn't easy · There's a business centre for working guests, room service, a 24-hour reception, a coffee shop, laundry service (extra charge), and airport and railway-station transfers (extra charge) · Free Wi-Fi covers both the rooms and common areas, and many reviews praise it as stable and usable, which is something working guests care about · To be straight about it, this hotel doesn't have a full gym or spa like bigger hotels, so the strength here is having the basics covered rather than luxury.

Food and the restaurant — the hotel has a restaurant serving Thai, Asian and international dishes, and breakfast is included in the room rate on many packages · Reviews on the breakfast split fairly clearly into two camps, which is worth knowing before you set expectations · The praise side says breakfast offers both Thai and international choices, the taste is fine, it fills you up nicely before you set off, and some even call it a good breakfast for the price · The critical side says that more recently the buffet selection has looked thinner and less varied than before, perhaps because occupancy has been lower · A fair conclusion is that breakfast here is "just okay" — not somewhere you'd come specifically to eat, but not bad enough to avoid either · The upside is that the city-centre location helps a lot, because for other meals you can easily drive out to good restaurants in central Buriram — Isan eateries, noodle shops, cafés and the evening market · So a lot of people use the hotel breakfast as the convenient meal and then go hunt for good food outside for the rest, which is the charm of staying in the city centre.

Service — service is a point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews · A lot of staff are described as friendly, smiley and helpful, and quick to handle things — whether it's check-in/check-out, asking about places to visit, or calling a car · Some reviews say they got service beyond what they paid for, which is what makes people want to come back · To be fair, there are a few voices saying some staff's English is still limited, so a few foreign visitors had to communicate a bit more slowly, but for Thai guests there's basically no problem · The reception is open 24 hours, so you can check in late or arrive in the early morning — good for people driving long distances or taking an overnight train · Overall, service is a strong point that lifts the stay above what the star count suggests.

What real reviews say (both praise and criticism) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the city-centre location that gets you everywhere quickly by car, the wide free parking that's hard to find downtown, rooms that are clean and bigger than expected, air-con that cools fast, the saltwater pool that's gentle on the skin, friendly helpful staff, and the reassurance of an international-brand hotel at an accessible price · On the criticism side: the most-mentioned thing is the quality and variety of the breakfast buffet dropping off in some periods, and a few reviews feel the overall standard is starting to show some cost-cutting · Next are the fairly small lift, the location where — even though it's in the city — walking to restaurants at night without a car still isn't that convenient, and in the past there were reports of a power (transformer) issue, but that was a one-off · Most of these criticisms are things you can manage by setting expectations right and picking the package/room that fits your use, rather than big problems that keep people from returning — so it's no surprise the overall score is still good and it ranks among the top in town.

"Overall really good value for the price · clean room, lovely staff, easy parking · the only gripe was that the breakfast had fewer choices than I'd expected on the round I went — next time I might head out for some khao tom in town in the morning instead."

Price and value — the starting rate for a Standard room is about THB 1,100/night at normal prices (roughly the 31 US dollars several platforms quote), with the average around THB 1,400–1,600/night · Prices can climb to roughly THB 2,000–2,800+ during big events like a major football match or a MotoGP race, when the whole city fills up · Compared with other hotels in central Buriram, this price is good value in the accessible international-brand bracket, especially once you factor in the free parking, saltwater pool, breakfast and the reassurance of a brand name with a predictable standard · Compared with a luxury stadium-side hotel like Amari Buriram United, which costs more and focuses on activities at the stadium, this place suits people who want to be in the city centre and save money · And compared with the cheapest places in town, you pay a bit more here but get a proper standard and parking you can feel easier about · In short, it's an option where "price versus what you get" is fairly balanced for a city-sightseeing trip or a business trip.

Things to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoother · One, if you're driving yourself, this is the hotel's big advantage — make full use of the free parking and plan your routes to Phanom Rung, Prasat Muang Tam and Khao Kradong from the city with ease · Two, check clearly whether the package you book includes breakfast, because the price differs and the breakfast reviews are fairly mixed; if you're not fussed about breakfast in the hotel, pick the no-breakfast option and head out to eat in town · Three, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a higher floor or a non-road-facing side right when you book · Four, during big events (Buriram United home matches or MotoGP) the whole city fills up fast and prices jump sharply, so book several weeks to several months ahead · Five, go with free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet, and compare prices across platforms because discounts vary by period · Six, if you want the airport or railway-station transfer, give notice in advance because there's an extra charge.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Best Western Royal Buriram Hotel is the best fit for people who want to stay in central Buriram on an accessible budget, with international-brand standards and convenient free parking · A location that drives to the Lower Isan Cultural Centre, the King Rama I Monument, the railway station and the city markets in a few minutes, plus the saltwater pool and friendly service, make it a balanced, good-value option · If you're looking for the design of a luxurious newer hotel, full resort-style facilities, or a varied breakfast as the main draw, this might not be the answer, and you should consider a higher-tier hotel or staying by the stadium instead · But for a Lower Isan road trip, a business trip in the city, or anyone who wants the reassurance of a familiar brand at a friendly price — Best Western Royal Buriram answers that need well, and that's why it has stayed among the top hotels in town.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Best Western Royal Buriram Hotel

faq.q: Where is Best Western Royal Buriram Hotel · what's nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is at 332/22-23 Jira Road, Nai Muang Subdistrict, Muang Buriram District, in the city centre · The King Rama I Monument is about 1.3 km away (walkable), the Lower Isan Cultural Centre about 2.4 km, and Buriram railway station about 2.7 km · Chang Arena and the Chang International Circuit are about a 10–15 min drive, while Buriram Airport is about 34.5 km (~37 min drive).

faq.q: What's the starting price at Best Western Royal Buriram · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,100/night for a Standard King (average around THB 1,400–1,600) · There's Standard King, Standard Twin, Deluxe King and a Family room · During big events like home matches or MotoGP, prices jump sharply and rooms fill up fast, so compare several platforms and book ahead.

faq.q: Does the hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor saltwater pool that's gentle on skin and eyes, good for kids to play and for cooling off · and free on-site parking, a big advantage for people road-tripping around Lower Isan, because finding a city-centre place with parking this convenient isn't easy · Free Wi-Fi throughout, and many reviews say the signal is stable.

faq.q: Who is Best Western Royal Buriram for?
faq.a: A great fit for business travellers, families road-tripping around Lower Isan, and people who want to stay in the city centre on an accessible budget with international-brand standards · It has free parking, a saltwater pool, and a location that drives to everything quickly · If you're looking for luxurious design or full resort-style facilities, a higher-tier hotel or staying by the stadium might suit you better.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Best Western Royal Buriram?
faq.a: There's both Thai and international breakfast, included in the room rate on many packages · Reviews are fairly mixed — some praise the taste as fine and filling, but in some periods the buffet selection looks thinner · The upside is that the city-centre location makes it easy to head out to good restaurants, so many people use the hotel breakfast as the convenient meal and go hunt for food in town for the rest.

faq.q: How do I get from the railway station or airport to the hotel?
faq.a: Buriram railway station is about 2.7 km away, a few minutes by car · Buriram Airport (BFV) is about 34.5 km, roughly a 37 min drive · The hotel offers airport and railway-station transfers (extra charge) with advance notice · The reception is open 24 hours, so you can check in late or arrive in the early morning.
